title: Tate endomorphism ideals and traces of mixed commutators
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $V$ a $k$-vector space and $A\subset V$ a $k$-linear subspace. Write $X\prec Y$ for $\dim_k((X+Y)/Y)<\infty$. Define subspaces of $\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ by
$$E=\{T:T(A)\prec A\},\quad E_1=\{T:T(V)\prec A\},\quad E_2=\{T:\dim_kT(A)<\infty\},\quad E_0=E_1\cap E_2.$$
Then $E$ is a unital $k$-subalgebra; $E_1,E_2$ are two-sided ideals in $E$, and $E_1+E_2=E$. Every product $ST$ with $S\in E_2$ and $T\in E_1$ has finite-dimensional image. In particular each element of $E_0$ is finite-potent, and its finite-potent trace [lem-pc-finite-potent-trace-calculus] is a $k$-linear function on $E_0$. If either $(S,T)\in E_0\times E$ or $(S,T)\in E_1\times E_2$, then $[S,T]=ST-TS\in E_0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}([S,T])=0$.

source.place: §1, p. 151, Propositions 1 and 2, with the finite-rank-product observation underlying T4

proof.text: Finite-error witnesses. By [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], images and finite sums of finite-dimensional spaces are finite-dimensional: apply a linear map to a finite spanning list, or concatenate the lists. A subspace $L$ of a finite-dimensional space $W$ is also finite-dimensional: [lem-trf-vector-subspace-complement] supplies $W=L\oplus Q$, and the linear projection $W\to L$, defined by the unique decomposition, maps a finite spanning list onto a spanning list of $L$. Now $X\prec Y$ is equivalent to $X\subseteq Y+W$ for some finite-dimensional $W$: in the forward direction lift a finite spanning list of $(X+Y)/Y$ to $X+Y$ and let $W$ be its span; conversely the images of a spanning list of $W$ span $(Y+W)/Y$, whose subspace $(X+Y)/Y$ is finite-dimensional. We use these explicit witnesses below.

The algebra $E$. Zero, the identity and all scalar multiples of the identity preserve $A$. If $R(A)\subseteq A+W_R$ and $T(A)\subseteq A+W_T$, then $(R+T)(A)\subseteq A+W_R+W_T$, $(cR)(A)\subseteq A+W_R$ for $c\in k$, and $(RT)(A)\subseteq R(A)+R(W_T)\subseteq A+W_R+R(W_T)$. The displayed error spaces are finite-dimensional by their finite spanning lists [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], as in step 1. These inclusions prove closure under addition, scalar multiplication, multiplication and hence subtraction; thus $E$ is a unital $k$-subalgebra.

The ideal $E_1$. If $T(V)\subseteq A+W_T$, the same containment holds for $T(A)$, so $E_1\subseteq E$. Sums and scalar multiples remain in $E_1$ using sums of the finite error spaces, with zero error for the zero map. For $R\in E$, choose $R(A)\subseteq A+W_R$. Then $(RT)(V)\subseteq R(A)+R(W_T)\subseteq A+W_R+R(W_T)$ and $(TR)(V)\subseteq T(V)\subseteq A+W_T$. The error spaces have finite spanning lists [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Therefore $E_1$ is a $k$-linear two-sided ideal of $E$; the right-multiplication argument even permits arbitrary $R\in\operatorname{End}_k(V)$.

The ideal $E_2$. If $T(A)$ is finite-dimensional then $T(A)\subseteq A+T(A)$, so $E_2\subseteq E$. Sums, negatives and scalar multiples have image on $A$ contained in the corresponding finite sums of images, so $E_2$ is a $k$-linear subspace. If $R\in E$ and $R(A)\subseteq A+W_R$, then $(RT)(A)=R(T(A))$ is finite-dimensional and $(TR)(A)\subseteq T(A)+T(W_R)$ is finite-dimensional. Here images and sums have the explicit finite spanning lists of step 1, and subspaces of such spaces are finite-dimensional by the complement argument there. Thus $E_2$ is a two-sided ideal of $E$; left multiplication permits arbitrary $R$.

The sum of the ideals. Apply [lem-trf-vector-subspace-complement] to $A\subseteq V$, without a finite-dimensionality assumption, and write $V=A\oplus B$. Define $P(a+b)=a$; uniqueness of the decomposition proves that $P$ is $k$-linear, $P(V)=A$ and $(1-P)(A)=0$. For $T\in E$ choose $T(A)\subseteq A+W$. Then $PT\in E_1$ because its image lies in $A$, and $((1-P)T)(A)\subseteq(1-P)(W)$ is finite-dimensional by [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] and step 1. Consequently $T=PT+(1-P)T\in E_1+E_2$. The reverse inclusion follows from steps 2–4, proving $E_1+E_2=E$.

Finite-rank products. For $S\in E_2$ and $T\in E_1$, choose $T(V)\subseteq A+W$. Then $(ST)(V)\subseteq S(A)+S(W)$, a sum of two finite-dimensional spaces. Its subspace $(ST)(V)$ is finite-dimensional by step 1. This proves the product assertion, with the order $S\in E_2$ on the left and $T\in E_1$ on the right. In particular $U\in E_0$ satisfies $U^2(V)$ finite-dimensional, so is finite-potent in the sense of [lem-pc-finite-potent-trace-calculus].

Linearity on $E_0$. Steps 3–4 show $E_0=E_1\cap E_2$ is a $k$-linear subspace. For $U,V\in E_0$, each of $U^2,UV,VU,V^2$ has finite-dimensional image by step 6. Apply the final assertion of [lem-pc-finite-potent-trace-calculus] to the two operators $U,V$ to obtain $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(U+V)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(U)+\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(V)$. Its homogeneity clause gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(cU)=c\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(U)$, including $c=0$. Thus the trace restricts to a $k$-linear function on $E_0$.

Commutators with $E_0$. Let $S\in E_0$ and $T\in E$. Both $ST$ and $TS$ belong to both ideals by steps 3–4, so $[S,T]\in E_0$. In particular $ST$ is finite-potent by step 6. The cyclicity clause of [lem-pc-finite-potent-trace-calculus], with $a=T:V\to V$ and $b=S:V\to V$, gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(ST)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(TS)$. The linearity proved in step 7 now yields $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(ST-TS)=0$.

source.place: §1, p. 151, Proposition 2, first case; T5 on p. 150

proof.text: Mixed commutators. Let $S\in E_1$ and $T\in E_2$. We have $ST\in E_1$ by right stability of $E_1$, and $ST\in E_2$ by left stability of $E_2$. Also $TS\in E_1$ by left stability of $E_1$ (since $T\in E$), and $TS\in E_2$ by right stability of $E_2$ (since $S\in E$). Thus both products and their difference belong to $E_0$. Step 6 shows $TS$ has finite-dimensional image; hence it is finite-potent, taking exponent one. Apply the cyclicity clause of [lem-pc-finite-potent-trace-calculus] with $a=S$ and $b=T$ to get equal traces of $TS$ and $ST$. Step 7 gives zero trace for $ST-TS$. This proves the second case without assuming that $ST$ itself has finite-dimensional image.
